# MP v2 — First-class co-op (execution plan)

## Context

Online multiplayer v1 shipped and is live (v0.13.0, deployed + prod-validated on Vercel + Neon + Fly). It works, but landed with six documented scope-cuts that make co-op feel like a demo rather than the real game:

1. **Vehicles can't be boarded online** — rafts/ships are gated off under server authority (a mounted pose is server-driven, which fought the client-owned pose stream).
2. **Arrows don't replicate** — only the `arrowHit` event crosses the wire, so remote players never see arrows fly.
3. **Progression only credits the host** — server rooms accrue advancements/stats to the primary player.
4. **Kill credit defaults to the host** — indirect kills (arrow, pet, explosion) credit the primary, not the killer.
5. **Pets follow the nearest player**, not their owner.
6. **No way to remove a griefer** — the game server has a `kick` endpoint but no player-facing control.
7. **SP worlds don't follow you across devices** — the cloud-save transport is built but unwired.

**Intended outcome:** close all of them so co-op plays like single-player and the account layer feels complete. Target release **v0.14.0**.

The engine is already per-player-shaped for most of this (save v17): `PlayerState` owns `stats`/`advancements`/`inventory`/`xp` and serializes per-player; `recordEvent`/`evaluateAdvancements` are per-`PlayerState`; `removeMobAt` already has an (unused) `creditTo` param with XP/loot wired; the renderer draws straight off `state.vehicles`/`state.projectiles`. Most work is **threading the acting player through a few boundaries** and **adding wire channels that copy the existing mob-replication skeleton**.

**All seams below were re-verified against current `main` (2026-07-04, HEAD 727ab9d).** Path/line corrections vs the prior draft are folded in. Key gotcha: engine subsystems live under **`lib/game/engine/systems/`** and **`lib/game/engine/state.ts`** (not `lib/game/systems/` / `lib/game/state.ts`); the renderer is **`lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts`**; `MobPose` is defined in **`lib/net/protocol.ts:113`** (imported by `server/room.ts`).

## Delivery decisions (user-confirmed 2026-07-04)

- **One branch `feat/mp-v2`**, phased commit slices, **one PR** at the end (matches v1 + the "big work = one reviewable unit" rule).
- **Straight through** all four phases this session; run the **full verify gate green at each phase boundary**; commit focused slices; **stop before push** (no push/PR/tag without explicit user ask — standing preference).
- **Phase 4 is in scope** for v0.14.0.
- **`PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1 → 2** (`lib/net/protocol.ts:20`): additive wire, but version-locked at the door — `server/index.ts:93` checks the hello `protocol` field and `:95` checks `claims.pv`; both must equal `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, so a stale v1 client is cleanly refused during a v2 rollover.
- **No save-format or worldgen bump** — per-player stats/advancements + placed vehicles already persist in v17. Phase 4 adds one optional *local-manifest* field (`WorldMeta.cloudId`), which is not the world save format.

---

## Phase 1 — Live replication: vehicles + arrows

**Goal:** remote players see arrows fly and boats move; boarding works in MP. Copy the mob-replication skeleton (`collectMobPoses` `server/room.ts:472` → `MobPose` `protocol.ts:113` → `upsertReplicaMob` `NetworkSession.ts:248`, which also builds a per-entity interpolation buffer at `:280`). Render side already consumes `state.vehicles`/`state.projectiles` (`GameRenderer.ts:215,217`).

- **Un-gate boarding under server authority:** `GameEngine.ts:859` — `if (this.authority !== "server" && !this.replica && tryBoardAimedVehicle(state, player)) break;`. Remove the authority/replica guard (a right-click arrives as a networked `placeBlock` cmd; ship step-on already fires server-side in `tickVehicles`). Keep `applyRemotePose`'s mounted reject (`GameEngine.ts:448-449`).
- **Vehicle pose channel (mirror mobs):** new `VehiclePose { id, kind, x, y, z, yaw, riderId }` in `protocol.ts`; `collectVehiclePoses()` in `server/room.ts` beside `collectMobPoses`; carry it in a new per-tick `TickMessage` field. `upsertReplicaVehicle()` in `NetworkSession.ts` populating `state.vehicles` (reuse `restoreVehicle`, `lib/game/engine/systems/vehicles.ts:55`).
  - **Fix the existing omission:** `applyWorldSync` (`NetworkSession.ts:231-246`) restores mobs but silently drops the `vehicles` field that `WorldSync` already carries (`protocol.ts:108`). Restore `sync.vehicles` there too (full-keyframe path); the new `VehiclePose` channel handles per-tick deltas.
- **Mounted-player feedback (the reason boarding was cut):** the server owns a mounted player's position, driven by their input intents through `tickVehicles` (intents already arrive via `setPlayerInput` on every pose). Extend `SelfDelta` (`protocol.ts:122`) with `mountedVehicleId?: string | null` + authoritative `x/y/z/yaw` (emitted only while mounted). Diff/emit in `buildSelfDelta` against `conn.shadow` (`server/room.ts:502-536`, shadow type `:63-75`; note the full-resend reset at `room.ts:334`). Apply in `applySelfDelta` (`NetworkSession.ts:288`) — snap `self.position` like the `forcePose` handler. In the replica `step()` loop (`GameEngine.ts:519-524`) skip `tickPlayerMotion` for the local player when `mountedVehicleId !== null` so the server-driven position wins (kills rubber-band). **This is the one genuinely novel piece — build it first, test it hard.**
- **Arrow pose channel:** new `ProjectilePose { id, x, y, z, vx, vy, vz }` (velocity so `projectileVisuals` orientation works unchanged); `collectProjectilePoses()` — **no deadband**, emit all live ones every tick, prune-by-absence (arrows are ephemeral/fast); `upsertReplicaProjectile()` populating `state.projectiles`; snap-per-frame, skip interpolation (arrows outrun the ~125 ms buffer delay). `WorldSync` gains a `projectiles` keyframe field for join-time state.
- **Tests:** `server/room.test.ts` (vehicle + projectile poses broadcast; mounted self-delta emitted only while mounted). `NetworkSession.test.ts` (upsert vehicle/projectile from wire; mounted snap; `applyWorldSync` restores vehicles). `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (boarding accepted under server authority; replica skips local motion when mounted). **Docs:** `protocol.md` (new poses + PROTOCOL_VERSION 2), `online.md` (rafts/ships boardable — drop the v1 caveat), `architecture.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Phase 2 — Per-player attribution: progression, kill-credit, pets

**Goal:** each player earns their own advancements/stats and gets credit for their own kills; pets follow their owner. Attribution (C) and kill-credit (D) are the same change — thread the **acting player** through two boundaries.

- **Attribute events to the actor (C):** widen the emit boundary to `emit(event, actorId?: PlayerId)` (`GameEngine.ts:1150`), threaded from sites that already hold a `player` (the whole `dispatch` switch; `removeMobAt`'s receiver). `observeProgress(event, actorId?)` (`:1166`) resolves `actor = actorId ? getPlayer(state, actorId) : primary`, then `recordEvent(actor, event)` + `evaluateAdvancements(actor)` **unchanged** (already per-`PlayerState`). Preserve the recursion guard (`:1154` — skips re-entry on `advancementUnlocked`) and route its re-emit to the same actor.
- **Kill credit (D):** `removeMobAt` (`GameEngine.ts:1296`) already resolves `receiver = creditTo ?? primary` (`:1302`) and calls `awardXp(receiver, …)` (`:1312`) — it just has **zero callers passing `creditTo`**. Pass the killer at all sites:
  - Melee → `player`, via the `attack` handler (`GameEngine.ts:869-887`, which already holds `player` but passes `this.removeMobAt` bare at `:883`).
  - Arrows/spears → a new `owner?: PlayerId` on `ProjectileState` (`lib/game/engine/state.ts:146`; today only `fromPlayer: boolean`) and a **brand-new** `owner?: PlayerId` on `ThrownSpearState` (`:166`, which has *no* owner field today). Capture at `spawnArrow` (`lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts:23`, extend `SpawnArrowOptions` `:4-10`) and at spear-throw (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`, invoked from `GameEngine.ts:847`). Forward through the widened `removeMobAt` dep signatures at the death sites: `projectileAI.ts:124` (projectile-vs-mob, currently 1-arg) and `spears.ts:93`.
  - Explosion / mob-vs-mob death sweep (`mobAI.ts:504-512`, death at `:511`) → the crediting player (pet kills credit `mob.owner`; TNT credits its igniter).
  - The same resolved actor feeds C's attribution.
- **Per-player progression on the wire (C):** extend `SelfDelta` with `advancements?: string[]` + changed `stats?: {id,value}[]`; diff in `buildSelfDelta` against new `conn.shadow` slots; apply in `applySelfDelta` onto `self.advancements`/`self.stats` (reuse `serializeStats` `save.ts:506`, `restoreStats` `:515`, `restoreAdvancements` `:527`). Makes each client's own advancement/stat snapshot correct.
- **Pet owner-follow (E):** in the `faction === "ally"` branch of `tickMobs` (`mobAI.ts:345-361`), resolve `owner = mob.owner ? getPlayer(state, mob.owner) : null` (helper at `players.ts:68`; `mob.owner` exists at `state.ts:107`) and target `owner.position` for follow/teleport instead of `anchor` (`nearestPlayerTo`, `:306`/`players.ts:87`). Fallback when the owner is offline: idle (not nearest). `anchor`/`nearestPlayerTo` stays for wild-animal flee.
- **Tests:** `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (two players each earn own advancements; a 2nd player's kill credits them not primary; arrow/pet kill credits shooter/owner; pet follows owner over a nearer stranger). Existing advancements/combat/mobAI suites stay green. **Docs:** `architecture.md` (per-player attribution), `online.md` (drop the "progression accrues to primary" caveat), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Phase 3 — Owner controls: kick + roster

**Goal:** the world owner sees who's connected and can remove someone, in-game. Use a **protocol message**, not a web→game admin bridge (the bridge would add cross-deployment coupling against the stateless design; the protocol path reuses the owner-gate already in `handleMessage`).

- **Wire:** add `KickMessage { t: "kick"; targetId }` to the `ClientMessage` union (`protocol.ts:74`) + a case in `readClientMessage` (`:256-284`, validate `isStr(m.targetId)`). Server `handleMessage` kick case mirrors the existing owner-gate (`room.ts:306`: `if (conn.role !== "owner") return; this.kick(message.targetId)`); reuses `Room.kick` (`room.ts:252`, already closes + `leave` + broadcasts `playerLeft`) and `conn.role` (from `claims.role`, `room.ts:220` / `tickets.ts:26`).
- **Role to the client:** add `role` to `WelcomeMessage` (`protocol.ts:80-92`), filled from `claims.role` where WELCOME is built (`room.ts:231-245`); expose `session.role`. Self-contained for the panel.
- **Roster to the UI:** add a roster subscription to `NetworkSession` copying the chat/status pattern (`subscribeChat`/`subscribeStatus` at `NetworkSession.ts:478-485`, backing `Set`s `:111-112`). New `Set` + `subscribeRoster()` firing on `applyRoster` (`:215`), `playerJoined` (`:375`), `playerLeft` (`:381`); `session.roster()` from `state.players` + `names` (`:123`, `playerName` `:489`); `session.kick(targetId)`.
- **UI:** new `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx` copying the `ChatPanel`/`ConnectionStatus` shape (props `{ session }`, `useEffect` subscribe→unsubscribe cleanup). Render online-only at `MinecraftGame.tsx:156-157` (beside the existing `{online && …}` panels). Lists players; owners get a Kick button per non-self id.
- **Tests:** `protocol.test.ts` (kick validation), `server/room.test.ts` (owner kick via message; member's kick ignored), `NetworkSession.test.ts` (roster/kick send + subscription fires), `RosterPanel.test.tsx`. **Docs:** `protocol.md` (kick message + role), `online.md`/`manual.md` (owner controls), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Phase 4 — SP cloud-save autosync

**Goal:** a signed-in player's single-player worlds sync to the cloud and follow them across devices. Transport (`cloudSaves.ts` `pushSave`/`pullSave`, gzip, `x-base-updated-at` stale guard, 409→`"conflict"`) and server (`worldsService` `get/putSaveBlob` LWW, `sp-cloud` kind) are **already built and tested** — this is wiring. **Opt-in per world** (explicit "Upload to cloud"), not auto-upload of every local world.

- **Local↔cloud link:** add optional `WorldMeta.cloudId` (`lib/game/worlds.ts:21-36`). The sanitizer `sanitizeWorld` (`:88-111`) rebuilds a fresh object with only known keys, so `cloudId` must be **explicitly copied through** `sanitizeWorld` *and* `createWorld` (`:134-162`), else it's silently dropped. Parameterize `createOnlineWorld` (`onlineClient.ts:24-44`, currently hardcodes `kind: "mp"` at `:36`) to send `kind: "sp-cloud"` (server already accepts both — `worldsService.createWorld` validates the union, `:85`).
- **World list (`WorldSelect.tsx`):** `WorldSummary.kind` already exists (`worldsService.ts:21`) but the UI ignores it (`:181-241` renders every online world identically). Split `listOnlineWorlds()` by `kind`: `"mp"` → existing Online Worlds join section (unchanged); `"sp-cloud"` → merge into the local list (materialize a local `WorldMeta` + pull on first play). Add an "Upload to cloud" action on a local world that creates its `sp-cloud` row and links `cloudId`.
- **Push on save (`useMinecraftGame.ts`):** persistence runs through `persistGame` (`:87`, calls `writeSave`) at the autosave/gameOver/unmount/quit sites (`:300,329,395,524`), **all already `if (!online)`-guarded**. Alongside those, add a **debounced** `pushSave(cloudId, api.serialize())` when the world is cloud-linked and signed in. `beforeunload` cloud flush is best-effort only (`sendBeacon` can't set the required headers) — flush on quit/unmount instead.
- **Pull on play (`GameShell.tsx`):** cloud-linked worlds need an **async pull gate** before entering play. Reuse the `connecting`/`connectError` "Joining…" modal (`:80-81`, `:193-207`) that `playOnline` already uses — but resolve to the **SP** screen `{ name: "play", … }` (`:23-27`), *not* `play-online` (`:104`). `pullSave` → `writeSave(worldSaveKey, …)` → normal boot from disk.
- **Conflict (409):** `pushSave` returns `"conflict"`; surface keep-local (re-push after refreshing the base) vs adopt-remote (`pullSave`) via the existing `net-modal`/toast pattern.
- **Tests:** `worlds.ts` cloud-link round-trips the sanitizer; `WorldSelect.test.tsx` (sp-cloud split/merge); a `GameShell` async-pull test. `cloudSaves`/`worldsService` suites already cover transport/LWW. Optional e2e in `multiplayer.e2e.ts` (stack + pglite already wired). **Docs:** `online.md` (cloud saves live), `manual.md` (worlds across devices), `architecture.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

---

## Critical files

- **Protocol/wire:** `lib/net/protocol.ts` (PROTOCOL_VERSION 2; `VehiclePose`/`ProjectilePose`/`KickMessage`; `SelfDelta`/`WelcomeMessage`/`TickMessage`/`WorldSync` fields; validators), `lib/net/codec.ts` (unchanged).
- **Server:** `server/room.ts` (collect/broadcast poses, self-delta extensions, kick case, role in welcome), `server/index.ts` (unchanged — door lock already bumps with the constant).
- **Client session:** `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts` (upsert vehicle/projectile, mounted self-delta, roster/kick, role, `applyWorldSync` vehicles fix), `lib/net/NetworkSession.test.ts`.
- **Engine:** `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts` (un-gate boarding, replica mounted skip, `emit`/`observeProgress`/`removeMobAt` actor threading), `lib/game/engine/systems/{vehicles,projectileAI,spears,combat,mobAI,advancements}.ts`, `lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts` (`spawnArrow` owner), `lib/game/engine/state.ts` (`owner` on projectile/spear), `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts`.
- **Client UI/shell:** `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx` (new), `components/MinecraftGame.tsx`, `components/GameShell.tsx`, `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`.
- **SP save:** `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` (built), `lib/game/worlds.ts` (`cloudId` + sanitizer), `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` (push hook), `lib/online/onlineClient.ts` (sp-cloud create).
- **Docs:** `docs/protocol.md`, `docs/online.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/manual.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Verification

- **Per phase (the gate CI runs):** `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` — **assert real exit 0**, not just "0 fail" (the PGlite exit-99 lesson: unclosed fixtures exit 99 even when all tests pass; never gate on `bun test | tail`) — and `bun run build`. Add `bun run test:e2e` for phases touching renderer/input/shell (1, 3, 4).
- **Phase-specific unit tests** are the workhorse (headless two-player boarding, kill-credit attribution, per-player advancements, pet-follow) via `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` + fake-socket `server/room.test.ts`/`NetworkSession.test.ts`. Local-fixture states use the self-referential `state.player = state` / `GameState & PlayerState` cast pattern already in the suite.
- **End-to-end (live):** the two-browser pass from v1 — board a boat together, see arrows fly, each earn a distinct advancement, kick a third guest, and (Phase 4) create a cloud world on one device and open it on another. Prod stack (Vercel + Neon + Fly) already deployed.
- **Release (end of branch, after user review):** bump to **v0.14.0** (version bump + CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`→`[0.14.0]` roll + `chore(release)` commit + tag), matching the v0.13.0 flow. **Do not push/tag until the user asks.**

## Out of scope (future thrusts)

Client-side movement prediction/rollback (the hybrid model already gives smooth own-movement); interest management / chunk streaming; PvP tuning; public rooms / matchmaking / moderation; SP→MP world conversion. Foundation/licensing (OSS license via upstream PR) remains a separate track.

# MP v2 — First-class co-op (execution plan)

## Context

Online multiplayer v1 shipped and is live (v0.13.0, deployed + prod-validated on Vercel + Neon + Fly). It works, but landed with six documented scope-cuts that make co-op feel like a demo rather than the real game:

1. **Vehicles can't be boarded online** — rafts/ships are gated off under server authority (a mounted pose is server-driven, which fought the client-owned pose stream).
2. **Arrows don't replicate** — only the `arrowHit` event crosses the wire, so remote players never see arrows fly.
3. **Progression only credits the host** — server rooms accrue advancements/stats to the primary player.
4. **Kill credit defaults to the host** — indirect kills (arrow, pet, explosion) credit the primary, not the killer.
5. **Pets follow the nearest player**, not their owner.
6. **No way to remove a griefer** — the game server has a `kick` endpoint but no player-facing control.
7. **SP worlds don't follow you across devices** — the cloud-save transport is built but unwired.

**Intended outcome:** close all of them so co-op plays like single-player and the account layer feels complete. Target release **v0.14.0**.

The engine is already per-player-shaped for most of this (save v17): `PlayerState` owns `stats`/`advancements`/`inventory`/`xp` and serializes per-player; `recordEvent`/`evaluateAdvancements` are per-`PlayerState`; `removeMobAt` already has an (unused) `creditTo` param with XP/loot wired; the renderer draws straight off `state.vehicles`/`state.projectiles`. Most work is **threading the acting player through a few boundaries** and **adding wire channels that copy the existing mob-replication skeleton**.

**All seams below were re-verified against current `main` (2026-07-04, HEAD 727ab9d).** Path/line corrections vs the prior draft are folded in. Key gotcha: engine subsystems live under **`lib/game/engine/systems/`** and **`lib/game/engine/state.ts`** (not `lib/game/systems/` / `lib/game/state.ts`); the renderer is **`lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts`**; `MobPose` is defined in **`lib/net/protocol.ts:113`** (imported by `server/room.ts`).

# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. The transport is built and tested; surfacing it in the
world list / autosave UX is still to come.

## Playing online (client)

The menu's **Online Worlds** section (`WorldSelect`) lists every world the
signed-in user may play, creates new ones (same form as local worlds — the
row lives in Postgres, the game server hosts it), and mints invite links
(`/join/<token>` — the landing page resolves the token, signs the visitor in
as a guest if needed, and accepts the membership). Playing one runs
`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the
session's replica engine. The connection lifecycle (chat, ping badge,
disconnect modal, leave) lives in the session + two HUD components; the
architecture of the replica/routing/interpolation stack is in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#multiplayer-client-libnet).

v1 scope cuts to know about (all documented where they bite): rafts/ships
can't be boarded online (a mounted pose is server-driven, which would fight
the client-owned pose stream); in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only
their hits); advancements/stats don't accrue in server rooms; indirect mob
kills credit the primary player.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bun run db:migrate            # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
bun run server                # game server (ws://localhost:8080)
```

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — separate guest identities), create an online world in
the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

**[deploy.md](deploy.md) is the step-by-step first-time deploy runbook** (Neon
schema → Fly game server → Vercel web app, with a verify checklist and
troubleshooting). In short:

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server): shares `DATABASE_URL` and `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`
  with the web app (a mismatch on the latter = every join fails with close
  code 4000).

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

All admin endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN` (absent
`ADMIN_TOKEN` = always 403):

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this); unauthenticated.
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics: players, tick, `slowestTickMs`
  (against the 50 ms budget), and `kbOutPerSec` (downstream bandwidth). Watch
  these to set `MAX_ROOMS`.
- `GET /rooms/:id/log` — the room's rolling replay log (recent commands with
  their claimed eye pose + per-second pose anchors, `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE`
  entries). Feed a dump to `bun scripts/replay.ts dump.json` to reconstruct
  the command-driven state offline (edits/inventory/movement — mobs aren't
  reproduced; the live RNG is unseeded).
- `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId` — eject a player (fatal `4003`, no retry).

`PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the Playwright
multiplayer spec, and the two CLI clients: `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (one
client, joins/walks/tallies) and `bun scripts/loadSim.ts <url> <world> <N>
<seconds>` (N synthetic clients → server tick p95 + bandwidth, for capacity
tuning). Both mint their own ticket, so `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` must match; give
`loadSim` `ADMIN_TOKEN` too for the server-side stats.

### Runbook

- **A player is stuck / griefing.** The world owner revokes shared invite
  links from the menu ("Revoke links" on the world card — kills every
  outstanding link at once; existing members keep access). To force a live
  player out, `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`.
- **A redeploy.** SIGTERM drains every room (persist + close with `4005`);
  clients reconnect on the ladder to the new instance and re-sync. Loss is
  bounded to the last 60 s (the dirty-persist interval) even on a hard crash.
- **"How did this happen?"** Pull `/rooms/:id/log`, then `bun scripts/replay.ts`
  to replay the command stream against a fresh engine and diff the outcome.
- **Latency feels bad.** From a browser console, `window.__monecraft.net`
  `.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects delay to reproduce; set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` to bake it into a dev build.
- **Capacity.** Run `loadSim` at the target player count and watch
  `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` in `/rooms`; keep p95 well under 50 ms and set
  `MAX_ROOMS` so peak memory (~74 MB/room) fits the machine. Net constants
  (deadbands, keyframe/persist intervals, reconnect ladder) live in
  [tuning.md](tuning.md#multiplayer-networking).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

1	# Wire protocol (v1)
2	
3	The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
4	source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
5	`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
6	door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.
7	
8	## Transport & framing
9	
10	WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
11	discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
12	`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
13	terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
14	binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
15	contract, not the encoding.
16	
17	## Handshake
18	
19	1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
20	2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
21	   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
22	   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
23	3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).
24	
25	A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
26	worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
27	the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.
28	
29	## Steady state
30	
31	**Client → server**
32	
33	- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
34	  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
35	  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
36	  distance stats, and fall damage.
37	- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
38	  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
39	  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
40	  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
41	- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.
42	
43	**Server → client**
44	
45	- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
46	  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
47	  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
48	  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
49	  sent only on change.
50	- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
51	  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.
52	
53	Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
54	and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.
55	
56	## Reconnect
57	
58	The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
59	walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
60	**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
61	new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
62	new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
63	same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with
64	`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
65	path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
66	world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
67	exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.
68	
69	## Close codes
70	
71	| Code | Meaning                                           | Client retries? |
72	| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
73	| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          | no (fatal)      |
74	| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         | no (fatal)      |
75	| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      | no (fatal)      |
76	| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) | no (fatal)      |
77	| 4004 | idle timeout                                      | yes (ladder)    |
78	| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) | yes (ladder)    |
79	| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              | no (fatal)      |
80	| 1006 | abnormal close (network drop)                     | yes (ladder)    |
81	
82	## Trust model
83	
84	The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
85	in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
86	thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
87	claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
88	invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
89	rewind validation would need.

# Wire protocol (v1)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**

- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.

**Server → client**

- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
  sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Reconnect

The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with
`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.

## Close codes

# Wire protocol (v1)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**

- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.

**Server → client**

- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
  sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with

path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh

exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.

35:- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command, playerId?)` (the id says whose intent it is; the SP shell omits it), advances `step(dt, input?)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`), the world size is overridable for fast headless tests, and four options shape multiplayer hosting: `authority` ("local" honors `pause` and freezes the world while the primary player is dead — the single-player feel; "server" ignores pause and never freezes a shared world), `headless` (skips snapshot building — a server room has no React shell), `replica` (a client mirror of a server room: steps only the local player's prediction, cosmetic mining, and the day clock — mobs/spawns/vitals arrive over the wire instead of simulating), and `bootPlayer: false` (construct with an empty players map — a server room before the first join, a replica before its `welcome`; the snapshot stays a stub until `addPlayer` seats the primary). `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` are the join/leave surface (join restores the player's persisted v17 slice; leave serializes it back for the world save); `setPlayerInput(playerId, input)` stores each client's latest intent packet; `applyRemotePose` is the server-side gate on client-owned movement (speed/vertical clamps, teleport rejection, and a synthesized move summary so hunger/stats/fall damage stay server-authoritative); the `routeDispatch` hook lets a session intercept every dispatch — how online play reroutes gameplay commands up the wire while the input controller and UI stay unchanged.
95:- `remotePlayerVisuals.ts` — the **other** players in an online world: one humanoid per non-primary entry in `state.players` (reusing `playerModel.ts`/`playerPose.ts` + the skin palettes), gait animated from observed movement, topped by a procedural canvas name-tag sprite. Names/skins arrive via the `GameRenderer.remotePlayerInfo` lookup (the shell points it at the session roster); pure state-mirroring like `mobVisuals.ts` — the renderer neither knows nor cares that the poses come from interpolation buffers.
117:## Multiplayer client (`lib/net/`)
119:Online play mounts the **same** shell/renderer/audio/input stack on a different engine: `connectNetworkSession(url, ticket)` (`NetworkSession.ts`) performs the hello → welcome → gzipped world-sync handshake, then constructs a **replica** engine (`replica: true, bootPlayer: false` — worldgen from the server's seed is byte-identical thanks to `lib/world/noise.ts`, the world sync applies the block diff/containers/mobs on top). `useMinecraftGame` accepts the session via its `online` option: the replica engine is mounted instead of constructing one, localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), replicated server events join the local event drain (so toasts/audio/particles treat them like local ones), and `session.afterFrame` runs each rAF.
121:- **Command routing** rides the engine's `routeDispatch` hook: presentation commands (`pause`, toggles, camera) run on the replica; gameplay commands go up the wire as `cmd` envelopes carrying the claimed eye pose (`selectSlot` optimistically does both). 122:- **Own movement is client-owned** (the one hybrid concession): the local player simulates normally for zero-latency feel, streaming pose + intents at tick rate; the server clamps (speed/vertical/teleport → `forcePose` snap-back) and owns the consequences (hunger, fall damage, stats). - **Command routing** rides the engine's `routeDispatch` hook: presentation commands (`pause`, toggles, camera) run on the replica; gameplay commands go up the wire as `cmd` envelopes carrying the claimed eye pose (`selectSlot` optimistically does both). The input controller and every UI panel dispatch exactly as in single-player — they can't tell the difference.
- **Own movement is client-owned** (the one hybrid concession): the local player simulates normally for zero-latency feel, streaming pose + intents at tick rate; the server clamps (speed/vertical/teleport → `forcePose` snap-back) and owns the consequences (hunger, fall damage, stats). Everything else is server-authoritative — the replica's own mining is **cosmetic** (progress caps just short of breaking; the true break arrives via the block journal), and `self` deltas overwrite the local player's vitals/inventory through the same validators saves use.
- **Remote entities render in the past**: per-entity pose ring buffers (`interpolation.ts`) are sampled at estimated-server-time − 125 ms (clamp, never extrapolate), fed by 20 Hz player poses and deadbanded 10 Hz mob poses + 5 s keyframes; `clock.ts` keeps the server-time estimate via ping/pong RTT EWMA.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Online co-op parity — vehicles & arrows (protocol v1→v2)**: rafts and ships are now boardable in a shared world, and in-flight arrows are replicated (not just their hits). Vehicles and arrows travel on their own per-tick channels (`vp`/`prj`, mirroring the mob-pose skeleton) and the join world-sync, so the existing renderer draws them unchanged. A **mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their position (driven from their input intents) and streams it on the private `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + authoritative position), so the client replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than rubber-banding against the boat — and the server no longer answers a mounted player's (expected-rejected) pose with a `forcePose` snap-back. The version bump means a stale v1 client is cleanly refused at the door during a rollover. Single-player is unchanged; the boarding gate that made vehicles single-player-only is lifted.

feat(online): replicate vehicles + arrows and enable boarding in co-op (protocol v2)

Online multiplayer v1 shipped with rafts/ships boardable in single-player
only and in-flight arrows unreplicated (remote players saw the hit, never the
arrow). Both were cut because a mounted rider's position is server-driven,
which fought the client-owned pose stream, and because neither entity had a
wire channel. This closes the first two MP v2 scope-cuts.

Vehicles and arrows now travel on their own per-tick channels (`vp`/`prj`)
plus the join world-sync, copying the mob-pose skeleton: the server collects
poses (vehicles deadbanded — a parked boat costs nothing; arrows sent in full
every tick and pruned by absence with one trailing empty frame), the client
upserts them straight into state.vehicles/state.projectiles keyed by server
id, and the existing renderer draws them unchanged. This also restores the
world-sync's `vehicles` field, which the client had silently dropped.

Boarding is un-gated: it runs wherever the dispatch switch runs (single-player
and the authoritative server — a right-click is already a networked placeBlock
cmd; the replica never dispatches it locally). While mounted the server owns
the rider's position via tickVehicles and streams it on the private SelfDelta
(mountedVehicleId + authoritative x/y/z), so the replica adopts the mount state
and stops integrating its own motion rather than rubber-banding against the
boat. The server also suppresses forcePose for a mounted player's expected-
rejected pose (that reject means "ignore the stream", not "you desynced").

PROTOCOL_VERSION 1 -> 2 so a stale v1 client is cleanly refused at the door
during a rollover. No save/worldgen bump. Single-player behaviour unchanged.
EOF

you only see your own. Pets follow **their owner**, not the nearest player.

# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. The transport is built and tested; surfacing it in the
world list / autosave UX is still to come.

## Playing online (client)

The menu's **Online Worlds** section (`WorldSelect`) lists every world the
signed-in user may play, creates new ones (same form as local worlds — the
row lives in Postgres, the game server hosts it), and mints invite links
(`/join/<token>` — the landing page resolves the token, signs the visitor in
as a guest if needed, and accepts the membership). Playing one runs
`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the
session's replica engine. The connection lifecycle (chat, ping badge,
disconnect modal, leave) lives in the session + two HUD components; the
architecture of the replica/routing/interpolation stack is in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#multiplayer-client-libnet).

Boarding works online (protocol v2): a mounted rider's position is
server-owned and streamed on the `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + `x/y/z`),
so the replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than
rubber-banding against the boat. Vehicles and in-flight arrows replicate on
their own tick channels (`vp`/`prj`), mirroring the mob-pose skeleton.

Remaining v1 scope cuts (closed in later MP v2 phases): advancements/stats
don't yet accrue in server rooms, and indirect mob kills credit the primary
player.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bun run db:migrate            # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
bun run server                # game server (ws://localhost:8080)
```

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — separate guest identities), create an online world in
the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

**[deploy.md](deploy.md) is the step-by-step first-time deploy runbook** (Neon
schema → Fly game server → Vercel web app, with a verify checklist and
troubleshooting). In short:

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server): shares `DATABASE_URL` and `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`
  with the web app (a mismatch on the latter = every join fails with close
  code 4000).

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

All admin endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN` (absent
`ADMIN_TOKEN` = always 403):

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this); unauthenticated.
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics: players, tick, `slowestTickMs`
  (against the 50 ms budget), and `kbOutPerSec` (downstream bandwidth). Watch
  these to set `MAX_ROOMS`.
- `GET /rooms/:id/log` — the room's rolling replay log (recent commands with
  their claimed eye pose + per-second pose anchors, `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE`
  entries). Feed a dump to `bun scripts/replay.ts dump.json` to reconstruct
  the command-driven state offline (edits/inventory/movement — mobs aren't
  reproduced; the live RNG is unseeded).
- `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId` — eject a player (fatal `4003`, no retry).

`PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the Playwright
multiplayer spec, and the two CLI clients: `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (one
client, joins/walks/tallies) and `bun scripts/loadSim.ts <url> <world> <N>
<seconds>` (N synthetic clients → server tick p95 + bandwidth, for capacity
tuning). Both mint their own ticket, so `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` must match; give
`loadSim` `ADMIN_TOKEN` too for the server-side stats.

### Runbook

- **A player is stuck / griefing.** The world owner revokes shared invite
  links from the menu ("Revoke links" on the world card — kills every
  outstanding link at once; existing members keep access). To force a live
  player out, `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`.
- **A redeploy.** SIGTERM drains every room (persist + close with `4005`);
  clients reconnect on the ladder to the new instance and re-sync. Loss is
  bounded to the last 60 s (the dirty-persist interval) even on a hard crash.
- **"How did this happen?"** Pull `/rooms/:id/log`, then `bun scripts/replay.ts`
  to replay the command stream against a fresh engine and diff the outcome.
- **Latency feels bad.** From a browser console, `window.__monecraft.net`
  `.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects delay to reproduce; set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` to bake it into a dev build.
- **Capacity.** Run `loadSim` at the target player count and watch
  `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` in `/rooms`; keep p95 well under 50 ms and set
  `MAX_ROOMS` so peak memory (~74 MB/room) fits the machine. Net constants
  (deadbands, keyframe/persist intervals, reconnect ladder) live in
  [tuning.md](tuning.md#multiplayer-networking).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

36:- `state.ts` — `GameState` holds the **players map** (`players: Map<PlayerId, PlayerState>`; single-player is the one-entry case) beside the world: mobs, vehicles, and thrown spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, containers, world timers. `PlayerState` owns everything per-player: avatar pose, inventory/armor/hotbar, vitals, effects/xp/stats/advancements, death/respawn, mining/fishing/vehicle, per-player UI flags, per-player timers, live input. Plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
64:**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new kind requires entries in all seven exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `FACTION_BY_KIND`, `MOB_DROPS`, `MOB_XP`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).
74:**Advancements & statistics.** Progression meta (`systems/advancements.ts`) hangs off the **single `GameEngine.emit` chokepoint** every system already emits through: `emit` pushes the event for the shell, then runs `observeProgress` — `recordEvent` folds it into the `state.stats` counters (a `Map<string, number>`), and `evaluateAdvancements` unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed, adding it to `state.advancements` (a `Set`) and emitting `advancementUnlocked` (the one event type `emit` skips, to avoid recursing). The advancement set is a **declarative `{ stat, threshold }` registry**, so unlock is uniform and adding one is a single row with no logic. Tick-driven display stats (distance, play time) bump directly in `step` via `recordTick`, off the unlock path. Both `stats` and `advancements` persist in save v13 and, like `xp` and unlike `effects`, are **kept across death** (`clearEffects` never touches them). The L-key overlay (`AdvancementsPanel`) reads detail through `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render — only the open flag and the unlocked **count** ride the snapshot, so play never churns it with stat values the HUD doesn't show.
87:- **Per-voxel lighting**: the world/glass materials are patched via `onBeforeCompile` (`patchVoxelLighting`) to consume the baked `aLight` attribute — they gate the scene-lit colour by sky exposure (caves go dark) and add block light back as an albedo-tinted glow (torches/lava light the dark). **Day/night needs no uniform and no re-mesh**: the scene sun + hemisphere already scale with `daylight` in `syncDayNight`, so a sky-exposed surface dims at night through the scene lights while caves stay dark regardless. The patch anchors on stable `ShaderChunk` includes; the e2e "renders without errors" smoke test guards it against a Three.js bump.

feat(online): per-player progression, kill credit, and pet owner-follow

Online v1 rooms tracked no progression (advancements/stats accrued to the
nonexistent primary player), credited every indirect kill to the host, and
made pets trail the nearest player instead of their owner. This closes those
three co-op scope-cuts. Single-player is unchanged (it is the one-player case).

Attribution threads the acting player through the one emit chokepoint:
emit(event, actorId?) resolves the scorer as the explicit actor (a kill's
killer, a death's victim), else whoever's per-player stepPlayer/dispatch is
running (a new transient `actingPlayer`), else the primary. So each player's
mining/kills/crafts/deaths score to them, and a playerless room with no
attributable actor scores nothing — correct. A replica never scores; the
server owns progression and streams each player's advancements and event-
driven stats back on the SelfDelta (the two continuous display stats — play
time, distance — accrue client-side via recordTick, so they aren't sent).

Kill credit resolves through a new session-only MobState.lastHitByPlayer,
stamped by every player-attributed hit (melee, player arrow, thrown spear,
and a pet's bite → its owner). removeMobAt reads it, so even a delayed sweep
death (daylight burn, explosion after a softening hit) pays the right player
its loot and XP. Arrows and spears carry an `owner` for this.

Pets now follow their OWNER (getPlayer(mob.owner)) rather than the nearest
player, idling when the owner is offline. Advancement-unlock events are tagged
with the earning player so a co-op client only toasts its own.
EOF

# Wire protocol (v2)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**

- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.

**Server → client**

- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, vp?, prj?, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since
  last tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob
  poses (~10 Hz), **vehicle poses** (`vp`, deadbanded — a parked boat costs
  nothing; vehicles never despawn so no absence-pruning), **arrow poses**
  (`prj`, the full live set every tick — arrows are few and fast, so they snap
  and prune by absence; one trailing empty `prj` clears the last one), the day
  clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-authoritative delta of
  YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…), sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

**Vehicles & mounted riders (v2).** A vehicle's pose (`VehiclePose`: id, kind,
x/y/z, yaw, riderId) replicates on `vp` and in the join `worldSync` (keyed by
server id, so per-tick deltas line up). Arrows (`ProjectilePose`: id, x/y/z,
vx/vy/vz — velocity so the client orients the mesh) replicate on `prj`. A
**mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their
position (`tickVehicles` drives it from their input intents), so the pose
stream is rejected without a `forcePose` correction, and the `SelfDelta`
carries `mountedVehicleId` (on mount/dismount) plus the authoritative `x/y/z`
(while mounted). The replica adopts that mount state and snaps to the position,
skipping its own motion integration until it dismounts.

Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp`/`vp`/`prj` are shed
(events and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Reconnect

The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with
`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.

## Close codes

| Code | Meaning                                           | Client retries? |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          | no (fatal)      |
| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         | no (fatal)      |
| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      | no (fatal)      |
| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) | no (fatal)      |
| 4004 | idle timeout                                      | yes (ladder)    |
| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) | yes (ladder)    |
| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              | no (fatal)      |
| 1006 | abnormal close (network drop)                     | yes (ladder)    |

## Trust model

The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
rewind validation would need.

# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. The transport is built and tested; surfacing it in the
world list / autosave UX is still to come.

## Playing online (client)

The menu's **Online Worlds** section (`WorldSelect`) lists every world the
signed-in user may play, creates new ones (same form as local worlds — the
row lives in Postgres, the game server hosts it), and mints invite links
(`/join/<token>` — the landing page resolves the token, signs the visitor in
as a guest if needed, and accepts the membership). Playing one runs
`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the
session's replica engine. The connection lifecycle (chat, ping badge,
disconnect modal, leave) lives in the session + two HUD components; the
architecture of the replica/routing/interpolation stack is in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#multiplayer-client-libnet).

Boarding works online (protocol v2): a mounted rider's position is
server-owned and streamed on the `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + `x/y/z`),
so the replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than
rubber-banding against the boat. Vehicles and in-flight arrows replicate on
their own tick channels (`vp`/`prj`), mirroring the mob-pose skeleton.

Progression is per-player: each player earns their own advancements/stats
(the engine attributes an emitted event to whoever's step/dispatch is running,
so a co-op room scores every player independently) and gets credit for their
own kills — melee, arrow, spear, or a pet's bite, tracked on the mob as
`lastHitByPlayer` so even a delayed sweep death (burn, explosion) credits the
right player. The `SelfDelta` syncs each client's advancement set and
event-driven stats (the two continuous display stats — play time, distance —
accrue client-side). Advancement toasts are tagged with the earning player, so
you only see your own. Pets follow **their owner**, not the nearest player.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bun run db:migrate            # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
bun run server                # game server (ws://localhost:8080)
```

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — separate guest identities), create an online world in
the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

**[deploy.md](deploy.md) is the step-by-step first-time deploy runbook** (Neon
schema → Fly game server → Vercel web app, with a verify checklist and
troubleshooting). In short:

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server): shares `DATABASE_URL` and `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`
  with the web app (a mismatch on the latter = every join fails with close
  code 4000).

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

All admin endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN` (absent
`ADMIN_TOKEN` = always 403):

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this); unauthenticated.
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics: players, tick, `slowestTickMs`
  (against the 50 ms budget), and `kbOutPerSec` (downstream bandwidth). Watch
  these to set `MAX_ROOMS`.
- `GET /rooms/:id/log` — the room's rolling replay log (recent commands with
  their claimed eye pose + per-second pose anchors, `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE`
  entries). Feed a dump to `bun scripts/replay.ts dump.json` to reconstruct
  the command-driven state offline (edits/inventory/movement — mobs aren't
  reproduced; the live RNG is unseeded).
- `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId` — eject a player (fatal `4003`, no retry).

`PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the Playwright
multiplayer spec, and the two CLI clients: `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (one
client, joins/walks/tallies) and `bun scripts/loadSim.ts <url> <world> <N>
<seconds>` (N synthetic clients → server tick p95 + bandwidth, for capacity
tuning). Both mint their own ticket, so `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` must match; give
`loadSim` `ADMIN_TOKEN` too for the server-side stats.

### Runbook

- **A player is stuck / griefing.** The world owner revokes shared invite
  links from the menu ("Revoke links" on the world card — kills every
  outstanding link at once; existing members keep access). To force a live
  player out, `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`.
- **A redeploy.** SIGTERM drains every room (persist + close with `4005`);
  clients reconnect on the ladder to the new instance and re-sync. Loss is
  bounded to the last 60 s (the dirty-persist interval) even on a hard crash.
- **"How did this happen?"** Pull `/rooms/:id/log`, then `bun scripts/replay.ts`
  to replay the command stream against a fresh engine and diff the outcome.
- **Latency feels bad.** From a browser console, `window.__monecraft.net`
  `.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects delay to reproduce; set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` to bake it into a dev build.
- **Capacity.** Run `loadSim` at the target player count and watch
  `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` in `/rooms`; keep p95 well under 50 ms and set
  `MAX_ROOMS` so peak memory (~74 MB/room) fits the machine. Net constants
  (deadbands, keyframe/persist intervals, reconnect ladder) live in
  [tuning.md](tuning.md#multiplayer-networking).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

Online worlds are shared worlds that live on a server and hold **2–8 players** —
private co-op with people you invite, not public matchmaking. Everything offline
stays exactly as it is: local worlds never need an account or a connection.

you've gone online. **New Online World** uses the same form as a local world

clipboard — send it to your friends. Invite links expire after a while; copy a
fresh one any time.

guest if you're new), and adds the world to your **Online Worlds** list — click
its card to play. The world is yours to rejoin from that list from then on;

lines: - **Remote entities render in the past**: per-entity pose ring buffers (`interpolation.ts`) are sampled at estimated-server-time − 125 ms (clamp, never extrapolate), fed by 20 Hz player poses and deadbanded 10 Hz mob poses + 5 s keyframes; `clock.ts` keeps the server-time estimate via ping/pong RTT EWMA.

- **Vehicles & arrows replicate like mobs** (protocol v2): the replica never simulates them — `upsertReplicaVehicle`/`upsertReplicaProjectile` write `state.vehicles`/`state.projectiles` straight from the `vp`/`prj` tick channels (and the join world-sync), keyed by server id, so the existing `vehicleVisuals`/`projectileVisuals` draw them unchanged. Both **snap** (no interpolation buffer — boats move slowly, arrows outrun the 125 ms delay). Boarding is a networked `placeBlock` cmd; while **mounted**, the server owns the rider's position (via `tickVehicles`) and streams it on the `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + `x/y/z`), so the replica skips its own motion integration and snaps — no rubber-band against the boat, and the server suppresses `forcePose` for the (expected) rejected mounted poses.

- **The replica outlives its socket**: a non-fatal drop runs a back-off reconnect ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS`) that mints a fresh ticket (the `reconnect` callback → `requestJoinTicket`) and redoes the handshake — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a new socket, re-syncing the same engine in place, so nothing above the session (renderer/HUD/engine) is torn down. `setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects symmetric send/receive delay for local testing (also `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS`).

lines: +- **Online co-op — in-game player list & owner kick**: every online world now shows a **player list** in the top-right corner, and the world **owner** gets a **Kick** button beside each other player to eject a griefer without leaving the world (free the cursor with `Esc` to click it — the panel sits above the pause overlay). It rides a new owner-only `kick` protocol message that the game server re-checks against the sender's signed ticket role (a member's forged kick is dropped, and you can't kick yourself), reusing the same in-process eject as the admin endpoint — no web→game admin bridge, so the game server stays stateless. The `welcome` frame now carries each player's own role.

- **Online co-op parity — per-player progression, kill credit & pets**: each player in a shared world now earns their **own** advancements and statistics (the engine attributes an emitted gameplay event to whoever's per-player step or command is running, so a co-op room scores everyone independently instead of accruing nothing) and gets credit for their **own** kills — melee, arrow, spear, or a companion pet's bite — tracked on the mob so even a delayed death (a daylight burn, an explosion softened by your earlier hit) credits the right player, paying them the loot and XP. Your advancement set and stats sync privately over the `SelfDelta`, advancement toasts are tagged so you only see your own, and **pets follow their owner** rather than trailing the nearest player. Single-player is unchanged.

- **Online co-op parity — vehicles & arrows (protocol v1→v2)**: rafts and ships are now boardable in a shared world, and in-flight arrows are replicated (not just their hits). Vehicles and arrows travel on their own per-tick channels (`vp`/`prj`, mirroring the mob-pose skeleton) and the join world-sync, so the existing renderer draws them unchanged. A **mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their position (driven from their input intents) and streams it on the private `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + authoritative position), so the client replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than rubber-banding against the boat — and the server no longer answers a mounted player's (expected-rejected) pose with a `forcePose` snap-back. The version bump means a stale v1 client is cleanly refused at the door during a rollover. Single-player is unchanged; the boarding gate that made vehicles single-player-only is lifted.
