The path is a protocol message, not a web->game admin bridge: a bridge would
couple the two deployments and add cross-service env against the game server's
stateless design. Instead a new owner-only `kick { targetId }` message reuses
the exact owner-gate the room already applies to setDifficulty/setGameMode —
the server re-checks the sender's signed ticket role, so a forged kick from a
member is dropped, and self-kick is a no-op. It calls the same in-process
Room.kick the admin endpoint does (fatal 4003 close, leave, persist).

The `welcome` frame now carries each player's own role, exposed as
`session.role`; the session gains `roster()`, a `subscribeRoster` that fires on
join/leave (copying the chat/status subscription shape), and `kick()`. A new
`RosterPanel` lists everyone (top-right HUD) and renders a Kick button per
other player for the owner only. It sits at z-index above the pause overlay so
the owner can free the cursor with Esc and click it without leaving the world.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the pushing client stops
syncing and warns (rather than clobber the other device), then adopts the
newer save on the next open.

**How it flows through the menu** (all opt-in per world):

- **Upload** — a local world's card gets an "Upload to cloud" action once
  you've gone online: it creates an `sp-cloud` world row, links it via
  `WorldMeta.cloudId` (a local-manifest field, not part of the save format),
  and pushes the current save. The card then reads "☁ Synced".
- **On another device** — your `sp-cloud` saves you haven't downloaded yet
  appear under **Cloud Saves**; **Download** materializes a local world (linked
  by `cloudId`) and opens it, pulling the blob in.
- **Open** — a cloud-linked world reconciles first (`pullCloudSaveIfNewer`):
  the remote is adopted only when it advanced past this device's sync cursor,
  so a world you played offline keeps its newer local progress instead of being
  overwritten by an older cloud copy. Reuses GameShell's "Opening…" gate.
- **Save** — `useMinecraftGame` mirrors each local autosave/quit up to the
  cloud when the world is `cloudId`-linked and the player is signed in
  (fire-and-forget so the fetch survives the unmount).

# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. The transport is built and tested; surfacing it in the
world list / autosave UX is still to come.

## Playing online (client)

The menu's **Online Worlds** section (`WorldSelect`) lists every world the
signed-in user may play, creates new ones (same form as local worlds — the
row lives in Postgres, the game server hosts it), and mints invite links
(`/join/<token>` — the landing page resolves the token, signs the visitor in
as a guest if needed, and accepts the membership). Playing one runs
`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the
session's replica engine. The connection lifecycle (chat, ping badge,
disconnect modal, leave) lives in the session + three HUD components
(`ChatPanel`, `ConnectionStatus`, `RosterPanel`); the architecture of the
replica/routing/interpolation stack is in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#multiplayer-client-libnet).

**Owner controls.** The `welcome` carries the recipient's `role` (from the
join ticket), exposed as `session.role`. `RosterPanel` lists everyone in the
world (top-right HUD) and, for the **owner** only, shows a Kick button per
other player — it sends a `kick` message that the server re-checks against the
sender's ticket role (a member's kick is dropped), reusing the same in-process
`Room.kick` as the admin endpoint. It renders above the pause overlay, so the
owner frees the cursor (Escape) and ejects a griefer without leaving. No
web→game admin bridge: the protocol path keeps the game server stateless.

Boarding works online (protocol v2): a mounted rider's position is
server-owned and streamed on the `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + `x/y/z`),
so the replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than
rubber-banding against the boat. Vehicles and in-flight arrows replicate on
their own tick channels (`vp`/`prj`), mirroring the mob-pose skeleton.

Progression is per-player: each player earns their own advancements/stats
(the engine attributes an emitted event to whoever's step/dispatch is running,
so a co-op room scores every player independently) and gets credit for their
own kills — melee, arrow, spear, or a pet's bite, tracked on the mob as
`lastHitByPlayer` so even a delayed sweep death (burn, explosion) credits the
right player. The `SelfDelta` syncs each client's advancement set and
event-driven stats (the two continuous display stats — play time, distance —
accrue client-side). Advancement toasts are tagged with the earning player, so
you only see your own. Pets follow **their owner**, not the nearest player.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bun run db:migrate            # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
bun run server                # game server (ws://localhost:8080)
```

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — separate guest identities), create an online world in
the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

**[deploy.md](deploy.md) is the step-by-step first-time deploy runbook** (Neon
schema → Fly game server → Vercel web app, with a verify checklist and
troubleshooting). In short:

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server): shares `DATABASE_URL` and `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`
  with the web app (a mismatch on the latter = every join fails with close
  code 4000).

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

All admin endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN` (absent
`ADMIN_TOKEN` = always 403):

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this); unauthenticated.
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics: players, tick, `slowestTickMs`
  (against the 50 ms budget), and `kbOutPerSec` (downstream bandwidth). Watch
  these to set `MAX_ROOMS`.
- `GET /rooms/:id/log` — the room's rolling replay log (recent commands with
  their claimed eye pose + per-second pose anchors, `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE`
  entries). Feed a dump to `bun scripts/replay.ts dump.json` to reconstruct
  the command-driven state offline (edits/inventory/movement — mobs aren't
  reproduced; the live RNG is unseeded).
- `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId` — eject a player (fatal `4003`, no retry).

`PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the Playwright
multiplayer spec, and the two CLI clients: `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (one
client, joins/walks/tallies) and `bun scripts/loadSim.ts <url> <world> <N>
<seconds>` (N synthetic clients → server tick p95 + bandwidth, for capacity
tuning). Both mint their own ticket, so `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` must match; give
`loadSim` `ADMIN_TOKEN` too for the server-side stats.

### Runbook

- **A player is stuck / griefing.** The world owner revokes shared invite
  links from the menu ("Revoke links" on the world card — kills every
  outstanding link at once; existing members keep access). To force a live
  player out, `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`.
- **A redeploy.** SIGTERM drains every room (persist + close with `4005`);
  clients reconnect on the ladder to the new instance and re-sync. Loss is
  bounded to the last 60 s (the dirty-persist interval) even on a hard crash.
- **"How did this happen?"** Pull `/rooms/:id/log`, then `bun scripts/replay.ts`
  to replay the command stream against a fresh engine and diff the outcome.
- **Latency feels bad.** From a browser console, `window.__monecraft.net`
  `.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects delay to reproduce; set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` to bake it into a dev build.
- **Capacity.** Run `loadSim` at the target player count and watch
  `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` in `/rooms`; keep p95 well under 50 ms and set
  `MAX_ROOMS` so peak memory (~74 MB/room) fits the machine. Net constants
  (deadbands, keyframe/persist intervals, reconnect ladder) live in
  [tuning.md](tuning.md#multiplayer-networking).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

### Cloud saves — your single-player worlds across devices

Signed in, you can make a **single-player** world follow you between browsers
and machines. On the world's card, **Upload to cloud** copies it to your
account (the card then reads **☁ Synced**), and from there every save syncs up
automatically as you play. On another device, your synced worlds appear under
**Cloud Saves** — **Download** brings one onto that device to play.

It's last-write-wins: if the same world is played on two devices, the most
recent save wins. Open a synced world and it always catches up to the latest
first; a world you played offline keeps its newer progress rather than being
overwritten by an older cloud copy. Local worlds you never upload stay entirely
offline, exactly as before — cloud saves are opt-in, one world at a time.

20:## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
22:- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms via `createAccumulator` from `lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts`, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `renderer.handleEvent` for particle bursts, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
23:- `components/GameShell.tsx` is the menu shell **above** `useMinecraftGame`: a profile-select → world-select → play state machine (profiles own worlds; see [save-format.md](save-format.md)) that runs the one-time legacy migration on mount and renders `MinecraftGame` keyed by `world.id` (+ a reload nonce). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset changes the key, so React unmounts the game subtree — running the effect cleanup that disposes renderer/audio/input and clears the rAF + autosave — and a fresh mount boots the next world, **no page reload**. The tab's active world is remembered in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes it while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. `useMinecraftGame` therefore takes the `world` + `profile` to play and persists to that world's own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key.
31:- Note for the React Compiler lint rules: consume the hook with destructuring (`const { … } = useMinecraftGame()`); property access on the result object can false-positive `react-hooks/refs`.
45:0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
68:**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
70:**Difficulty.** Orthogonal to the mode, `state.difficulty` (`peaceful`/`easy`/`normal`/`hard`, `lib/game/difficulties.ts`) decides _how hard_ survival is — it follows the same shape as game modes: an enum, an `isDifficulty` guard, `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` for the UI, and **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that systems read instead of the raw id. The seams: `spawnDirector.ts` gates the initial population + night director + dungeon spawners on `hostilesSpawn` and scales the cadence/cap; `mobAI.ts` multiplies every mob hit at the strike (templates untouched); `playerStats.ts` scales regen and runs the new **starvation** tick (hunger 0 chips to a per-level HP floor, lethal only on Hard, routed through the same floored/lethal damage paths as Poison/environment). Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` → a v9 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`) and is switchable in-game — `setDifficulty` (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`) just updates the value the directors read next tick, except dropping to Peaceful, which despawns the hostiles already present (a plain splice — no loot/XP, no false boss victory). The two axes don't cross-couple: spawning keys only on difficulty, threat/damage only on mode.
72:**Hardcore.** A per-world boolean (`state.hardcore`, persisted in save v10 + `WorldMeta`, **immutable** unlike mode/difficulty). The constructor resolves it first so it overrides the other axes — forced to Survival + Hard — and `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` early-return under it (the player-facing switchers are disabled; the engine's own death transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock). Death is permanent: the two lethal seams (`applyDamage`, `applyEnvironmentalDamage`) divert to `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()`, which sets the persisted `gameOver` flag and flips the player to **Spectator** (a free-cam over the dead world, invulnerable so mobs can't re-trigger it) instead of arming the respawn countdown — so a reloaded `gameOver` world boots straight into spectating (the constructor resolves `gameMode` to spectator; the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check leaves it un-teleported). The shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event so a tab-close still persists the dead world; the Game Over screen (`components/game/GameOverScreen.tsx`) owns navigation (spectate / quit / delete), and `pause` is blocked while `gameOver`. The hearts render in a withered palette (`lib/ui/hudPixels.ts`).
109:- Volume settings (`settings.ts`) persist under their own localStorage key (`minecraft_audio_v1`) — never part of the world save.
119:Online play mounts the **same** shell/renderer/audio/input stack on a different engine: `connectNetworkSession(url, ticket)` (`NetworkSession.ts`) performs the hello → welcome → gzipped world-sync handshake, then constructs a **replica** engine (`replica: true, bootPlayer: false` — worldgen from the server's seed is byte-identical thanks to `lib/world/noise.ts`, the world sync applies the block diff/containers/mobs on top). `useMinecraftGame` accepts the session via its `online` option: the replica engine is mounted instead of constructing one, localStorage persistence is skipped (the server owns the world), replicated server events join the local event drain (so toasts/audio/particles treat them like local ones), and `session.afterFrame` runs each rAF.

lines: +- **Cloud saves — single-player worlds across devices**: signed in, you can now make a single-player world follow you between browsers and machines. An **Upload to cloud** action on a world's card copies it to your account (the card then reads **☁ Synced**) and syncs every autosave up from then on; on another device your synced worlds appear under a **Cloud Saves** section to **Download** and play. It's last-write-wins with a safe open-time reconcile: opening a synced world adopts the newer cloud copy only when it actually advanced past this device — so a world you played offline keeps its newer progress instead of being clobbered — and a losing write during play warns you and stops syncing rather than overwriting the other device. Opt-in per world; worlds you never upload stay fully offline, and this is a local-manifest link (`WorldMeta.cloudId`) — the world save format is unchanged. Wires up the cloud-save transport that shipped as groundwork in v0.13.0.

- **Online co-op — in-game player list & owner kick**: every online world now shows a **player list** in the top-right corner, and the world **owner** gets a **Kick** button beside each other player to eject a griefer without leaving the world (free the cursor with `Esc` to click it — the panel sits above the pause overlay). It rides a new owner-only `kick` protocol message that the game server re-checks against the sender's signed ticket role (a member's forged kick is dropped, and you can't kick yourself), reusing the same in-process eject as the admin endpoint — no web→game admin bridge, so the game server stays stateless. The `welcome` frame now carries each player's own role.

- **Online co-op parity — per-player progression, kill credit & pets**: each player in a shared world now earns their **own** advancements and statistics (the engine attributes an emitted gameplay event to whoever's per-player step or command is running, so a co-op room scores everyone independently instead of accruing nothing) and gets credit for their **own** kills — melee, arrow, spear, or a companion pet's bite — tracked on the mob so even a delayed death (a daylight burn, an explosion softened by your earlier hit) credits the right player, paying them the loot and XP. Your advancement set and stats sync privately over the `SelfDelta`, advancement toasts are tagged so you only see your own, and **pets follow their owner** rather than trailing the nearest player. Single-player is unchanged.

- **Online co-op parity — vehicles & arrows (protocol v1→v2)**: rafts and ships are now boardable in a shared world, and in-flight arrows are replicated (not just their hits). Vehicles and arrows travel on their own per-tick channels (`vp`/`prj`, mirroring the mob-pose skeleton) and the join world-sync, so the existing renderer draws them unchanged. A **mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their position (driven from their input intents) and streams it on the private `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + authoritative position), so the client replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than rubber-banding against the boat — and the server no longer answers a mounted player's (expected-rejected) pose with a `forcePose` snap-back. The version bump means a stale v1 client is cleanly refused at the door during a rollover. Single-player is unchanged; the boarding gate that made vehicles single-player-only is lifted.

feat(cloud-saves): sync single-player worlds across devices

The cloud-save transport (gzipped SaveData blobs, last-write-wins) shipped as
groundwork in v0.13.0 but was never wired into the menu or autosave. This wires
it up so a signed-in player's single-player worlds can follow them across
devices, closing the last MP v2 scope-cut. Opt-in per world; a world you never
upload stays entirely offline, and the link is a local-manifest field
(WorldMeta.cloudId) — the world save format is unchanged.

- Upload: a local world's card gains "Upload to cloud" (once online is in use),
  which creates an sp-cloud world row, links it via cloudId, and pushes the
  current save; the card then reads "Synced". createOnlineWorld takes a kind.
- Download: sp-cloud worlds you don't have locally appear under a Cloud Saves
  section; Download materializes a local world (linked by cloudId) and opens it.
- Push on save: useMinecraftGame mirrors each local autosave/quit/game-over up
  to the cloud for a cloudId-linked, signed-in world (fire-and-forget so the
  fetch survives the unmount).
- Open reconcile: GameShell gates a cloud-linked world on pullCloudSaveIfNewer,
  which adopts the remote ONLY when it advanced past this device's sync cursor —
  so a world played offline keeps its newer local progress instead of being
  clobbered by an older cloud copy. Reuses the "Opening…" modal.
- Conflict: a losing push (409) warns once and stops syncing rather than
  overwriting the other device; the next open adopts their newer save.
EOF

All four MP v2 phases are implemented, pushed, and green. Here's where things stand.

## MP v2 complete — PR #44

All four phases landed on `feat/mp-v2` as focused commits, with the **full verify gate green at every phase boundary** (lint, typecheck, format, `bun test` real exit 0, build, e2e 20/20):

| Phase | Commit | What it closes |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — Vehicles + arrows** | `27c4be7` | Boats boardable online; arrows replicate. New `vp`/`prj` tick channels copy the mob skeleton; a mounted rider's position is server-owned and streamed on the `SelfDelta`, so the replica stops rubber-banding. `PROTOCOL_VERSION → 2`. |
| **2 — Per-player attribution** | `d9a77b9` | Each player earns their own advancements/stats; kill credit follows the actual killer (melee/arrow/spear/pet) via `MobState.lastHitByPlayer`; pets follow their owner. |
| **3 — Kick + roster** | `d71175c` | In-game player list + owner Kick button (new owner-gated `kick` message, `role` in the welcome, new `RosterPanel`). |
| **4 — SP cloud saves** | `6ae713c` | Single-player worlds follow a signed-in player across devices — opt-in Upload/Download, push-on-save, and a safe open-time reconcile that won't clobber offline progress. |

**Test coverage:** 1106 unit tests (was 1080 at v0.13.0) + 20 e2e, all green. Every new seam has focused tests — two-player boarding, kill-credit resolution, per-player advancements, pet owner-follow, owner-gated kick, roster subscription, the cloud reconcile logic, and the world-list split.

The PR describes the whole feature and is now complete across all four phases — CI (verify + e2e + CodeRabbit) is running on the push.

## What's left — your call

Per the plan, the **v0.14.0 release is gated on your review** — I have not cut it. Remaining before merge:

1. **Your review of PR #44** (and CodeRabbit's, once it runs).

The prod stack (Vercel + Neon + Fly) is already deployed, though the game server there still speaks protocol v1 until you redeploy it (the version bump refuses a stale client cleanly, so a rollover is safe).
3. **Cut v0.14.0** — version bump + roll `CHANGELOG [Unreleased] → [0.14.0]` + `chore(release)` commit + tag. Say the word and I'll do it.

Here's my honest read on where things stand and what's worth doing next.

## The lay of the land

MP v2 (v0.14.0) is **built and in review** — PR #44, all four phases + the CodeRabbit fixes, CI green. You've paused the release, so the co-op work is "done but not landed." Everything else on the board:

- **Close-out items for MP v2** (your timing): a real 2-browser gameplay pass on the new features, redeploy the Fly server to protocol v2, then merge + cut v0.14.0. The gameplay pass is the one recurring debt in this project — the roadmap notes it's been deferred every release, and the wolf/cat spawn bug that shipped is exactly the kind a manual pass catches. MP v2 has the *most* unverified surface yet (boat physics in MP, arrow visuals, kill-credit feel, kick UX, cross-device cloud sync).
- **New content**: a menu of deferred thrusts — a potions/enchants batch (Fire Aspect/Thorns/Night Vision/splash — quick wins on existing seams), a **drowned** hostile (leans on the aquatic update), rideable **mounts** (which would reuse the exact vehicle mount/ride/replication machinery I just extended for MP — high synergy, MP-ready almost for free), or bigger swings (Nether-like dimension, redstone-lite, slabs/stairs).

My honest recommendation: **harden and verify MP v2 before piling more on top of it.** It's a large, freshly-landed, mostly-unverified stack, and the highest-leverage thing I can actually do (a true 2-browser manual pass is your job, but I *can* extend the Playwright multiplayer e2e to drive the new features end-to-end — board a boat together, see arrows replicate, each earn a distinct advancement, owner-kick, a cloud-save round-trip). # MP v2 e2e Extension — Harness Map & Feature Reachability

## 1. `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` (read fully, 122 lines)

**Two-context setup.** Each guest is a separate `browser.newContext()` → `newPage()`, so they have isolated cookies/localStorage (independent guest accounts):

- Host: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts:37-39` `const hostContext = await browser.newContext(); const host = await hostContext.newPage();`
- Friend: `:78-80` same pattern for `friendContext`/`friend`.
- Teardown: `:119-120` `await hostContext.close(); await friendContext.close();`

**Boot gate** — the bar every online page must clear (`:24-28`):
```ts
async function waitForOnlineGame(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft !== undefined, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.net?.status() === "online", undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.renderer.renderedTriangles() > 0, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
}
```

**Invite→join flow** (menu-driven for the host, link-driven for the friend):
- Host seeds a profile via `addInitScript` writing `minecraft_profiles_v1` (`:42-49`), then `:52-62`: clicks **"Play online as guest"**, waits for **"Playing as guest"**, clicks `getByTestId("profile-host-profile")`, `getByTestId("new-online-world")`, fills `getByLabel("World name")`/`"World seed"`, clicks **"Creative mode"** then **"Create World"**.
- Invite is minted via `fetch`, NOT the clipboard button (headless can't read clipboard) — `:66-75`:
```ts
const worldId = await host.evaluate(async () => {
  const response = await fetch("/api/worlds");
  const { worlds } = (await response.json()) as { worlds: Array<{ id: string }> };
  return worlds[0].id;
});
const inviteToken = await host.evaluate(async (id) => {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/worlds/${id}/invites`, { method: "POST" });
  const { token } = (await response.json()) as { token: string };
  return token;
}, worldId);
```
- Friend joins by navigating to `/join/${inviteToken}` (`:81`), waits for `getByText(/You've joined/)`, clicks `getByRole("link", { name: "Open the game" })`, creates its profile via `getByLabel("Profile name")` + **"Create"**, then clicks `getByTestId(\`online-world-${worldId}\`)` (`:82-90`).

**Assertions:**
- Both replicas see 2 players (`:93-95`):
```ts
for (const page of [host, friend]) {
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.players.size === 2, undefined, { timeout: 15000 });
}
```
- Block-break reaches both — host aims straight down and holds mouse; a `blockChanges` entry must appear on BOTH clients, proving the server decided and broadcast the break (`:101-110`):
```ts

---

## 3. Test affordances / hooks

**`window.__monecraft` definition** — `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts:80-84`:
```ts
declare global {
  interface Window {
    __monecraft?: { engine: GameEngine; renderer: GameRenderer; input: InputController; audio: AudioDirector; net?: NetworkSession };

```
Assigned at `:331`: `window.__monecraft = { engine: gameEngine, renderer, input, audio, net: online ?? undefined };` and `delete`d on teardown (`:432`). So `net` is present only for online worlds. `giveCreativeItem` also exists on the hook return (`:466`) but is not on the window handle — a test reaches it via `engine.dispatch`.

**`forcePointerLock`** — declared `lib/game/input/inputController.ts:19`, implemented `:227-233`; it pokes the engine-facing `pointerLocked` flag without notifying React (so keys→engine and held-mouse→mining work in headless).

- `InventoryPanel.tsx:212/251/254` `chest-grid` / `storage-grid` / `hotbar-grid`

**`NetworkSession` public surface** — `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:80-109` (the `export type NetworkSession`):
```ts
export type NetworkSession = {
  readonly engine: GameEngine;
  readonly playerId: PlayerId;
  readonly role: "owner" | "member";                         // Phase 3
  subscribeChat(listener): () => void;
  subscribeStatus(listener): () => void;
  subscribeRoster(listener: () => void): () => void;          // Phase 3

  applyLook(deltaYaw: number, deltaPitch: number): void;

  setSimulatedLatency(ms: number): void;
  simulatedLatency(): number;

```
Yes — **all four Phase 3 additions exist**: `role` (`:83`), `roster()` (`:93`, impl `:576`), `kick()` (`:99-100`, impl `:577-579` sends `{ t: "kick", targetId }`), `subscribeRoster()` (`:88-89`, impl `:572-575`). `RosterMember` = `{ id, name }` (`:78`). Chat subscribe/sendChat and status subscribe were already present.

Key routing fact for driving commands: `engine.routeDispatch` (`:216-223`) sends everything up to the server **except** `LOCAL_COMMANDS` (`:73` — `toggleInventory`, `toggleAdvancements`, `toggleDebug`, `toggleCameraView`, `pause`, `resume`); `selectSlot` is applied optimistically AND sent. So `window.__monecraft.engine.dispatch({...})` (or `net.dispatch`, which just calls `engine.dispatch`, `:585-587`) is the way a test drives server-authoritative actions. The protocol decoder whitelists which cross the wire — `lib/net/protocol.ts` includes `selectSlot`(244), `creativeGiveItem`(264), `placeBlock`(277), `attack`(278), and top-level `kick`(316).

## 4. Reachability of the NEW MP v2 features

### 4a. Owner kick + roster — **fully e2e-testable, easy**

`RosterPanel` is rendered for every online session (not gated on pause) — `components/MinecraftGame.tsx:159` `{online && <RosterPanel session={online} />}`.

Selectors (`components/game/RosterPanel.tsx`):
- Container `:21`: `<div className="roster-panel" aria-label="Players in this world">` → `getByRole("region"?)`/`locator(".roster-panel")`. Title `:23` `Players ({members.length})`.

  Kick
</button>
```

`ConnectionStatus` on `"closed"` (`components/game/ConnectionStatus.tsx:24-35`):
```tsx

    <div className="net-modal" role="alertdialog" aria-label="Disconnected">

Also assertable purely via hooks: `host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.net.kick(<friendId>))` where friendId comes from `host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.net.roster())`. **Verdict: practical end-to-end, low effort.**

### 4b. Vehicle boarding — **NOT practical end-to-end; keep as unit tests**

Boarding routes through `placeBlock` → `tryBoardAimedVehicle` (`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:897`, within the `placeBlock` case `:879-906`). It requires **an existing vehicle the player is aiming at**. There is no seed hook: the replica never simulates vehicles (`state.vehicles = []` then only replicated in — `NetworkSession.ts:265-283`), and the host client IS a replica, so `window.__monecraft.engine` can't author a vehicle — a local `state.vehicles.push(...)` would be overwritten by the next server frame and wouldn't exist server-side to board.

To create one you must place it: `tryPlaceVehicle` (`GameEngine.ts:902`) needs a raft/ship item held and a right-click aimed at water, and water support is strict — `vehicleHasWaterSupport` requires Water below + Air at deck across all footprint corners (`lib/game/engine/systems/vehicles.ts:97-107`, gated by `canOccupy` `:121-133`). No server-side HTTP hook exists to spawn a vehicle (grep of `server/` shows only kick/pose/cmd, no vehicle-spawn endpoint). So an e2e would need: creative-give a raft, locate/craft water near spawn, aim precisely at the water surface, right-click to place, re-aim at the placed raft, right-click to board — all through real pointer math on a software renderer. **Verdict: leave to unit tests** (the boarding/mount/dismount logic already lives in `systems/vehicles.ts:135-205` with `server/room.ts` streaming `riderId` via `vp` poses and the rider's server-owned position via `SelfDelta.mountedVehicleId`, `NetworkSession.ts:382`). If any e2e coverage is wanted, assert only *replication of a vehicle pose* if one could be placed — but placement itself is the blocker.

There IS a creative-give command reachable through the session/engine: `creativeGiveItem` (command `lib/game/engine/commands.ts:36`, engine handler `GameEngine.ts:939-945` — **creative mode only**, item must be in `ITEM_DEF_BY_ID`), and it crosses the wire (`protocol.ts:264`). The hook `giveCreativeItem` (`useMinecraftGame.ts:466`) just does `engine.dispatch({ type: "creativeGiveItem", itemId })`, so a test does the same via `window.__monecraft.engine.dispatch(...)` (routes up because it's not in `LOCAL_COMMANDS`).

Firing: `attack` also crosses the wire (`protocol.ts:278`); the server's `attack` case fires a bow when the held slot is a bow (`GameEngine.ts:907-915`), and `tryFireBow` requires a bow in `selectedSlot` and ≥1 `arrow` in inventory (`lib/game/engine/systems/combat.ts:114-134`, `:118` `if ((countsById(...).get("arrow") ?? 0) < 1) return false`). The spawned projectile is server-simulated and replicated to every client via the per-tick `prj` set → `applyProjectiles` → `state.projectiles` (`NetworkSession.ts:288-315`, `:441`).

**Test recipe (host, Creative world):** `dispatch({type:"creativeGiveItem", itemId:"bow"})`, `dispatch({type:"creativeGiveItem", itemId:"arrow"})`, select the bow slot via `dispatch({type:"selectSlot", slot:N})`, then `dispatch({type:"attack"})`; assert on BOTH pages `expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.projectiles.length)).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. Caveats: creativeGiveItem lands the stack at the server-side selected slot, so confirm the bow ends up in the selected slot (or select it after the self-delta lands), and the arrow ttl/flight is short — poll quickly. **Verdict: feasible via hooks (no pointer aiming needed), moderate effort.**

### 4d. Cloud saves (sp-cloud) — **menu-flow, e2e-testable with existing testids**

This is entirely the WorldSelect menu against `/api/worlds` — no game session needed. The full mechanism is in `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`:
- **Upload:** each *local* world card renders an "Upload to cloud" button when `onlineUsed()` and no `cloudId` yet (`:227-234`) — no testid, select by text/title. It calls `uploadToCloud` (`:127-151`) → `createOnlineWorld({..., kind: "sp-cloud"})` + `pushSave` + `linkWorldCloud`; on success the card flips to `☁ Synced` badge (`:222-224`). Failure shows "Upload failed" (`:233`).
- **Cloud Saves section:** unlinked `sp-cloud` rows (`:157`, filtered out if already linked locally) render under `<h3>Cloud Saves</h3>` (`:255-268`) with the **testid** `data-testid={\`cloud-world-${world.id}\`}` (`:261`) and text "Download to this device". Clicking calls `onDownloadCloud` → `GameShell.downloadCloud` (`:124-142`) which `createWorld(..., { cloudId })` then opens it, pulling the newer save (`GameShell.openWorld` `:95-111`).

**Sign-in as guest:** `AccountPanel` button **"Play online as guest"** (`components/menu/AccountPanel.tsx:114-132`, calls `ensureSignedIn()`), status text becomes **"Playing as guest"** (`:93`). No testids in AccountPanel — drive by role/name and text, exactly as the MP test does at `multiplayer.e2e.ts:52-53`.

**Test recipe:** guest sign-in → create a **local** world (`new-world` testid) → open+quit once so a save exists (upload of a save-less world still links but pushes nothing — `WorldSelect.tsx:142`) → click "Upload to cloud" → assert `☁ Synced`. Note the identity subtlety: cloud rows are per-account, so cross-device download in a fresh context needs the *same* signed-in account (guest sessions differ per context) — either sign in a real account or assert within one context after deleting the local copy. `e2e/menu.e2e.ts` shows the local-world create/play/reload patterns to mirror (e.g. `:26-29`, `:78-90`). **Verdict: testable end-to-end within one signed-in identity; cross-device requires a real (non-guest) account.**

# Harden & verify MP v2 — end-to-end browser coverage for the new co-op features

## Context

MP v2 (PR #44, branch `feat/mp-v2`, all 4 phases + review fixes) is thoroughly covered by **unit/integration** tests (1107 pass), but the **browser e2e** still only exercises v1: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` drives invite → join → shared block-edit → chat, and nothing more. The new co-op surface — **owner kick / roster**, **arrow replication**, and **SP cloud saves** — has no end-to-end browser coverage.

This matters because this project's one recurring quality debt is the **perpetually-deferred manual gameplay pass** (the shipped wolf/cat spawn bug is the cautionary tale — unit tests passed because fixtures built the mobs directly; only a real play session would have caught it). A true 2-browser visual pass stays the user's job, but the practically-drivable new behaviors *can* be locked with automated e2e — the automated version of that pass. Adding it **de-risks the eventual merge/release** of a large, freshly-landed feature and lands the coverage **on `feat/mp-v2` so PR #44 itself gains it**.

**Verified during exploration:** the Phase 3 session API (`net.role`, `net.roster()`, `net.kick()`, `net.subscribeRoster()`) and the cloud-save testids (`cloud-world-<id>`) already exist, so **no app code changes are needed** — this is pure test authoring against the documented `window.__monecraft.{engine,net,renderer}` hooks and existing selectors.

## Approach

Add to **`feat/mp-v2`** (part of PR #44), not a new branch. Two pieces: extend the existing co-op journey test, and add a focused cloud-save spec. All driving goes through `window.__monecraft` and existing roles/testids, mirroring the patterns already in `multiplayer.e2e.ts`.

### 1. Extend `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` (the one co-op journey test) — roster, arrows, kick

The existing test already creates a **Creative** online world with two guests in it. Append three checks to that same flow (one expensive setup, reused). **Kick must be last** — it disconnects the friend.

- **Roster** (after the `players.size === 2` gate): assert `net.roster().length === 2` on both pages, and that the host — an **owner** — renders a Kick button: `host.getByRole("button", { name: /^Kick / })` visible (the `RosterPanel` owner control, `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx:30`). This proves `role`/`roster()`/`subscribeRoster` end-to-end and the owner-only UI gate.

- **Arrow replication** (Creative world → the `creativeGiveItem` hook, no pointer aiming needed): on the host,
  1. Aim roughly level so the arrow flies instead of burying instantly: `host.evaluate(() => { window.__monecraft.engine.state.player.pitch = 0; })`, brief settle.
  2. `engine.dispatch({ type: "creativeGiveItem", itemId: "bow" })` and `"arrow"` (both cross the wire — `protocol.ts` allow-list; server-side give lands at the player's `selectedSlot`, `GameEngine.ts` creative-give handler).
  3. `expect.poll` the self-delta'd inventory for the bow slot (`inventory.findIndex(s => s?.id === "bow")`), then `dispatch({ type: "selectSlot", index: <bowSlot> })`; `expect.poll` that an `arrow` is present too.
  4. `dispatch({ type: "attack" })` — the server fires the bow (`tryFireBow` needs a held bow + ≥1 arrow).
  5. Assert on **both** pages: `expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.projectiles.length)).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — proving the `prj` channel replicates the arrow to the remote replica.
  - This is the fiddliest check (inventory sync latency + short arrow lifetime). If it proves flaky, fall back to asserting the host-side spawn plus a `mobsKeyframe`-independent friend-side poll with a longer window; worst case, drop it and rely on the `prj` unit tests (`server/room.test.ts` broadcast + `NetworkSession.test.ts` upsert). Flag it in the commit if trimmed.

- **Owner kick** (final gameplay step, before the `errors` assertion): get the friend's id from the host roster (`net.roster().find(m => m.id !== net.playerId).id`), then `host.evaluate(id => window.__monecraft.net.kick(id), friendId)` — exactly what the RosterPanel button's `onClick` calls. Assert:
  - friend: `expect.poll(() => friend.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.net.status())).toBe("closed")` **and** `friend.getByRole("alertdialog", { name: "Disconnected" })` visible (the `net-modal` from `ConnectionStatus.tsx:24` on a fatal `CLOSE_KICKED`, which is in `FATAL_CLOSES` → no reconnect).
  - host: `expect.poll(() => host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.players.size)).toBe(1)`.
  - **Risk to check:** a server-initiated `4003` close should be a clean browser close (no console error), so the terminal `expect(errors).toEqual([])` still holds. If the browser logs a WS-close error, extend `watchErrors`'s filter (the same pattern it already uses for favicon 404s).

### 2. New `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts` — the SP cloud round-trip (menu flow, no game server)

Cloud saves are the **WorldSelect menu** against `/api/worlds` (the Next app + pglite) — no WS session. One signed-in guest, one context, simulating a second device by clearing the sync cursor:

1. Seed a profile via `addInitScript` (like the MP test), `goto("/")`, **"Play online as guest"** → "Playing as guest", click the profile.
2. Create a **local** world (`new-world` testid → `CreateWorldForm` → name/seed → "Create World") — this enters play.
3. In play, make a distinctive, assertable edit: aim down + hold mouse to break the block underfoot (the smoke-test pattern via `acquirePointerLock`), assert `blockChanges.changes().length > 0`, then Save & Quit (autosave writes the local save).
4. Back on the world list, the card now shows **"Upload to cloud"** (once `onlineUsed()`); click it, wait for the **"☁ Synced"** badge (`WorldSelect.tsx`). This creates the `sp-cloud` row, links `cloudId`, and pushes the save.
5. **Delete** the local world (Delete → confirm). The cloud row survives; the world now surfaces under **Cloud Saves** (`WorldSelect.tsx` filters out already-linked cloud worlds).
6. **Simulate a fresh device**: `evaluate(() => localStorage.removeItem("minecraft_cloud_stamps_v1"))` — clearing the per-device sync cursor so `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` will *adopt* on the next open (without this, same-cursor → keep-local → no pull; this is the honest single-context stand-in for a second device, since guest identities differ per context).
7. Fetch the cloud world's id (`fetch("/api/worlds")` → the `kind === "sp-cloud"` row), click `getByTestId(\`cloud-world-<id>\`)` → **Download** → `GameShell.downloadCloud` materializes a local world (linked by `cloudId`) and opens it, pulling the save.
8. Assert the world boots (`window.__monecraft` defined + `renderer.renderedTriangles() > 0`) **and the edit round-tripped**: `engine.state.blockChanges.changes().length > 0` — proving the save survived the push → delete → pull cycle (a fresh materialized world would be 0 until the pull adopts the cloud copy). Terminal `expect(errors).toEqual([])`.

### Deliberately out of scope for e2e: vehicle boarding

Not practically headless-drivable: boarding needs an existing vehicle the player aims at, and there's **no seed hook** — the client is a replica (its `state.vehicles` is overwritten by server frames each tick) and there's no server-side vehicle-spawn endpoint; placing one requires a held raft + a right-click aimed at water with strict water-support geometry, through pointer math on a software renderer. It stays covered by the **unit tests** already in place: `server/room.test.ts` (vehicle-pose broadcast, mounted self-delta) and `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (boarding accepted under server authority, replica skips local motion when mounted). The plan notes this gap explicitly rather than shipping a flaky boarding e2e.

## Critical files

# Harden & verify MP v2 — end-to-end browser coverage for the new co-op features

## Context

MP v2 (PR #44, branch `feat/mp-v2`, all 4 phases + review fixes) is thoroughly covered by **unit/integration** tests (1107 pass), but the **browser e2e** still only exercises v1: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` drives invite → join → shared block-edit → chat, and nothing more. The new co-op surface — **owner kick / roster**, **arrow replication**, and **SP cloud saves** — has no end-to-end browser coverage.

This matters because this project's one recurring quality debt is the **perpetually-deferred manual gameplay pass** (the shipped wolf/cat spawn bug is the cautionary tale — unit tests passed because fixtures built the mobs directly; only a real play session would have caught it). A true 2-browser visual pass stays the user's job, but the practically-drivable new behaviors *can* be locked with automated e2e — the automated version of that pass. Adding it **de-risks the eventual merge/release** of a large, freshly-landed feature and lands the coverage **on `feat/mp-v2` so PR #44 itself gains it**.

**Verified during exploration:** the Phase 3 session API (`net.role`, `net.roster()`, `net.kick()`, `net.subscribeRoster()`) and the cloud-save testids (`cloud-world-<id>`) already exist, so **no app code changes are needed** — this is pure test authoring against the documented `window.__monecraft.{engine,net,renderer}` hooks and existing selectors.

## Approach

Add to **`feat/mp-v2`** (part of PR #44), not a new branch. Two pieces: extend the existing co-op journey test, and add a focused cloud-save spec. All driving goes through `window.__monecraft` and existing roles/testids, mirroring the patterns already in `multiplayer.e2e.ts`.

### 1. Extend `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` (the one co-op journey test) — roster, arrows, kick

The existing test already creates a **Creative** online world with two guests in it. Append three checks to that same flow (one expensive setup, reused). **Kick must be last** — it disconnects the friend.

- **Roster** (after the `players.size === 2` gate): assert `net.roster().length === 2` on both pages, and that the host — an **owner** — renders a Kick button: `host.getByRole("button", { name: /^Kick / })` visible (the `RosterPanel` owner control, `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx:30`). This proves `role`/`roster()`/`subscribeRoster` end-to-end and the owner-only UI gate.

- **Arrow replication** (Creative world → the `creativeGiveItem` hook, no pointer aiming needed): on the host,
  1. Aim roughly level so the arrow flies instead of burying instantly: `host.evaluate(() => { window.__monecraft.engine.state.player.pitch = 0; })`, brief settle.
  2. `engine.dispatch({ type: "creativeGiveItem", itemId: "bow" })` and `"arrow"` (both cross the wire — `protocol.ts` allow-list; server-side give lands at the player's `selectedSlot`, `GameEngine.ts` creative-give handler).

  4. `dispatch({ type: "attack" })` — the server fires the bow (`tryFireBow` needs a held bow + ≥1 arrow).
  5. Assert on **both** pages: `expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.projectiles.length)).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — proving the `prj` channel replicates the arrow to the remote replica.
  - This is the fiddliest check (inventory sync latency + short arrow lifetime). If it proves flaky, fall back to asserting the host-side spawn plus a `mobsKeyframe`-independent friend-side poll with a longer window; worst case, drop it and rely on the `prj` unit tests (`server/room.test.ts` broadcast + `NetworkSession.test.ts` upsert). Flag it in the commit if trimmed.

  - host: `expect.poll(() => host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.players.size)).toBe(1)`.
  - **Risk to check:** a server-initiated `4003` close should be a clean browser close (no console error), so the terminal `expect(errors).toEqual([])` still holds. If the browser logs a WS-close error, extend `watchErrors`'s filter (the same pattern it already uses for favicon 404s).

### 2. New `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts` — the SP cloud round-trip (menu flow, no game server)

Cloud saves are the **WorldSelect menu** against `/api/worlds` (the Next app + pglite) — no WS session. One signed-in guest, one context, simulating a second device by clearing the sync cursor:

1. Seed a profile via `addInitScript` (like the MP test), `goto("/")`, **"Play online as guest"** → "Playing as guest", click the profile.
2. Create a **local** world (`new-world` testid → `CreateWorldForm` → name/seed → "Create World") — this enters play.
3. In play, make a distinctive, assertable edit: aim down + hold mouse to break the block underfoot (the smoke-test pattern via `acquirePointerLock`), assert `blockChanges.changes().length > 0`, then Save & Quit (autosave writes the local save).

Not practically headless-drivable: boarding needs an existing vehicle the player aims at, and there's **no seed hook** — the client is a replica (its `state.vehicles` is overwritten by server frames each tick) and there's no server-side vehicle-spawn endpoint; placing one requires a held raft + a right-click aimed at water with strict water-support geometry, through pointer math on a software renderer. ## Verification

- **Full gate** (I'm editing `.ts` e2e files): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` (real exit 0), `bun run build` — unchanged from green, since no product code moves.

# Harden & verify MP v2 — end-to-end browser coverage for the new co-op features

## Context

MP v2 (PR #44, branch `feat/mp-v2`, all 4 phases + review fixes) is thoroughly covered by **unit/integration** tests (1107 pass), but the **browser e2e** still only exercises v1: `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` drives invite → join → shared block-edit → chat, and nothing more. The new co-op surface — **owner kick / roster**, **arrow replication**, and **SP cloud saves** — has no end-to-end browser coverage.

This matters because this project's one recurring quality debt is the **perpetually-deferred manual gameplay pass** (the shipped wolf/cat spawn bug is the cautionary tale — unit tests passed because fixtures built the mobs directly; only a real play session would have caught it). A true 2-browser visual pass stays the user's job, but the practically-drivable new behaviors *can* be locked with automated e2e — the automated version of that pass. Adding it **de-risks the eventual merge/release** of a large, freshly-landed feature and lands the coverage **on `feat/mp-v2` so PR #44 itself gains it**.

**Verified during exploration:** the Phase 3 session API (`net.role`, `net.roster()`, `net.kick()`, `net.subscribeRoster()`) and the cloud-save testids (`cloud-world-<id>`) already exist, so **no app code changes are needed** — this is pure test authoring against the documented `window.__monecraft.{engine,net,renderer}` hooks and existing selectors.

## Approach

Add to **`feat/mp-v2`** (part of PR #44), not a new branch. Two pieces: extend the existing co-op journey test, and add a focused cloud-save spec. All driving goes through `window.__monecraft` and existing roles/testids, mirroring the patterns already in `multiplayer.e2e.ts`.

### 1. Extend `e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts` (the one co-op journey test) — roster, arrows, kick

The existing test already creates a **Creative** online world with two guests in it. Append three checks to that same flow (one expensive setup, reused). **Kick must be last** — it disconnects the friend.

- **Roster** (after the `players.size === 2` gate): assert `net.roster().length === 2` on both pages, and that the host — an **owner** — renders a Kick button: `host.getByRole("button", { name: /^Kick / })` visible (the `RosterPanel` owner control, `components/game/RosterPanel.tsx:30`). This proves `role`/`roster()`/`subscribeRoster` end-to-end and the owner-only UI gate.

- **Arrow replication** (Creative world → the `creativeGiveItem` hook, no pointer aiming needed): on the host,
  1. Aim roughly level so the arrow flies instead of burying instantly: `host.evaluate(() => { window.__monecraft.engine.state.player.pitch = 0; })`, brief settle.
  2. `engine.dispatch({ type: "creativeGiveItem", itemId: "bow" })` and `"arrow"` (both cross the wire — `protocol.ts` allow-list; server-side give lands at the player's `selectedSlot`, `GameEngine.ts` creative-give handler).
  3. `expect.poll` the self-delta'd inventory for the bow slot (`inventory.findIndex(s => s?.id === "bow")`), then `dispatch({ type: "selectSlot", index: <bowSlot> })`; `expect.poll` that an `arrow` is present too.
  4. `dispatch({ type: "attack" })` — the server fires the bow (`tryFireBow` needs a held bow + ≥1 arrow).
  5. Assert on **both** pages: `expect.poll(() => page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.projectiles.length)).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — proving the `prj` channel replicates the arrow to the remote replica.
  - This is the fiddliest check (inventory sync latency + short arrow lifetime). If it proves flaky, fall back to asserting the host-side spawn plus a `mobsKeyframe`-independent friend-side poll with a longer window; worst case, drop it and rely on the `prj` unit tests (`server/room.test.ts` broadcast + `NetworkSession.test.ts` upsert). Flag it in the commit if trimmed.

- **Owner kick** (final gameplay step, before the `errors` assertion): get the friend's id from the host roster (`net.roster().find(m => m.id !== net.playerId).id`), then `host.evaluate(id => window.__monecraft.net.kick(id), friendId)` — exactly what the RosterPanel button's `onClick` calls. Assert:
  - friend: `expect.poll(() => friend.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.net.status())).toBe("closed")` **and** `friend.getByRole("alertdialog", { name: "Disconnected" })` visible (the `net-modal` from `ConnectionStatus.tsx:24` on a fatal `CLOSE_KICKED`, which is in `FATAL_CLOSES` → no reconnect).
  - host: `expect.poll(() => host.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft.engine.state.players.size)).toBe(1)`.
  - **Risk to check:** a server-initiated `4003` close should be a clean browser close (no console error), so the terminal `expect(errors).toEqual([])` still holds. If the browser logs a WS-close error, extend `watchErrors`'s filter (the same pattern it already uses for favicon 404s).

### 2. New `e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts` — the SP cloud round-trip (menu flow, no game server)

Cloud saves are the **WorldSelect menu** against `/api/worlds` (the Next app + pglite) — no WS session. One signed-in guest, one context, simulating a second device by clearing the sync cursor:

1. Seed a profile via `addInitScript` (like the MP test), `goto("/")`, **"Play online as guest"** → "Playing as guest", click the profile.
2. Create a **local** world (`new-world` testid → `CreateWorldForm` → name/seed → "Create World") — this enters play.
3. In play, make a distinctive, assertable edit: aim down + hold mouse to break the block underfoot (the smoke-test pattern via `acquirePointerLock`), assert `blockChanges.changes().length > 0`, then Save & Quit (autosave writes the local save).
4. Back on the world list, the card now shows **"Upload to cloud"** (once `onlineUsed()`); click it, wait for the **"☁ Synced"** badge (`WorldSelect.tsx`). This creates the `sp-cloud` row, links `cloudId`, and pushes the save.
5. **Delete** the local world (Delete → confirm). The cloud row survives; the world now surfaces under **Cloud Saves** (`WorldSelect.tsx` filters out already-linked cloud worlds).
6. **Simulate a fresh device**: `evaluate(() => localStorage.removeItem("minecraft_cloud_stamps_v1"))` — clearing the per-device sync cursor so `pullCloudSaveIfNewer` will *adopt* on the next open (without this, same-cursor → keep-local → no pull; this is the honest single-context stand-in for a second device, since guest identities differ per context).
7. Fetch the cloud world's id (`fetch("/api/worlds")` → the `kind === "sp-cloud"` row), click `getByTestId(\`cloud-world-<id>\`)` → **Download** → `GameShell.downloadCloud` materializes a local world (linked by `cloudId`) and opens it, pulling the save.
8. Assert the world boots (`window.__monecraft` defined + `renderer.renderedTriangles() > 0`) **and the edit round-tripped**: `engine.state.blockChanges.changes().length > 0` — proving the save survived the push → delete → pull cycle (a fresh materialized world would be 0 until the pull adopts the cloud copy). Terminal `expect(errors).toEqual([])`.

### Deliberately out of scope for e2e: vehicle boarding

Not practically headless-drivable: boarding needs an existing vehicle the player aims at, and there's **no seed hook** — the client is a replica (its `state.vehicles` is overwritten by server frames each tick) and there's no server-side vehicle-spawn endpoint; placing one requires a held raft + a right-click aimed at water with strict water-support geometry, through pointer math on a software renderer. It stays covered by the **unit tests** already in place: `server/room.test.ts` (vehicle-pose broadcast, mounted self-delta) and `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (boarding accepted under server authority, replica skips local motion when mounted). The plan notes this gap explicitly rather than shipping a flaky boarding e2e.

## Critical files

- **`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`** — extend the single journey test with the roster, arrow, and (last) kick checks. Reuse `waitForOnlineGame`, `watchErrors`, `acquirePointerLock` (`e2e/helpers.ts`).
- **`e2e/cloudSaves.e2e.ts`** (new) — the guest-signin → create → play/edit → upload → delete → clear-cursor → download → assert-edit-survived round-trip. Reuse the profile-seed + guest-signin patterns from `multiplayer.e2e.ts` and the break-block pattern from `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts`.
- **`docs/testing.md`** — update the "Browser E2E (multiplayer)" row to note kick/roster + arrow replication; add a row (or note) for the cloud-save round-trip.
- No app-code changes and no CHANGELOG entry (test-only; the user-facing MP v2 CHANGELOG entries already exist on the branch).

Hooks/selectors to reuse (all confirmed present): `window.__monecraft.net` → `role`/`roster()`/`kick()`/`playerId`/`status()`/`sendChat`; `window.__monecraft.engine.dispatch(...)` for `creativeGiveItem`/`selectSlot`/`attack`; `RosterPanel` Kick button via `getByRole("button", { name: /Kick / })`; `ConnectionStatus` disconnect via `getByRole("alertdialog", { name: "Disconnected" })`; `cloud-world-<id>` / `new-world` / `new-online-world` testids.

## Verification

- **`bun run test:e2e`** — the whole Playwright suite green, including the extended multiplayer journey and the new cloud-save spec (run it a couple of times to shake out any timing flakiness, especially the arrow check).
- **Full gate** (I'm editing `.ts` e2e files): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test` (real exit 0), `bun run build` — unchanged from green, since no product code moves.
- **Land it:** commit on `feat/mp-v2`; **push to update PR #44** when you're ready (consistent with how the branch's slices have been pushed). The manual 2-browser visual pass on the new features remains yours to do before the release cut.

A point-blank arrow won't show mid-flight (its hit effect still replicates). I left it as-is and documented it; it's the kind of thing this verification pass exists to catch.

# Finish landing MP v2 — redeploy the game server to protocol v2

## Context

MP v2 merged to `main` with **PROTOCOL_VERSION 1 → 2**. Vercel auto-deployed the v2 web app to production, but the Fly game server (`monecraft-server`) still runs **v1** — and the protocol is hard-version-locked both ways, so the live server now *cleanly refuses* online play (a v2 web client's hello/ticket carries `pv=2`, which the v1 server rejects). Single-player is unaffected. This closes that gap: redeploy the Fly server to v2 so production online co-op works again, then verify the full stack. That unblocks the manual gameplay pass on the live deploy and the v0.14.0 release cut (both your call, not part of this).

Prod has ~no active users and the refusal is clean-by-design, so this is low-risk housekeeping — but leaving the deploy half-shipped is untidy, so it's the responsible next step before new feature work.

## Approach

Pure ops — **no code changes**. Deploy `main`'s `server/` (which already carries `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2`, `lib/net/protocol.ts:20`) to Fly using the committed config, then verify. Reuses the exact runbook in [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md).

1. **Prereqs** (read-only): we're on `main`, synced (done). Confirm `flyctl` is authed — `fly auth whoami` (`fly`/`flyctl` is installed at `/opt/homebrew/bin/fly`). If it's not logged in, you auth via `! fly auth login` before I proceed. The app's secrets (`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`) were set on the v0.13.0 deploy and **persist across a redeploy** — nothing to re-set, so no risk of the "#1 misconfiguration" (a `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` mismatch → close 4000).

2. **Deploy** (outward-facing, run after your go-ahead): from the repo root,
   `fly deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile`
   — builds and ships `main`'s v2 server code to `monecraft-server`. Fly does a rolling release; the version-lock means any lingering v1 client is refused cleanly during the swap (exactly what the bump was designed for).

3. **Verify** (no shared secret needed):
   - `curl https://monecraft-server.fly.dev/health` → `{"ok":true,"rooms":…}` (server up).
   - **Confirm it actually speaks v2** with a tiny WebSocket probe (only close codes, so no ticket/secret required): a `hello { protocol: 2, ticket: "bogus" }` must close with **4000** (bad ticket — the protocol matched the door), while a `hello { protocol: 1, … }` must close with **4001** (protocol mismatch). The server checks `message.protocol !== PROTOCOL_VERSION` *before* the ticket (`server/index.ts`), so those two close codes distinguish a v2 server from a v1 one. (`scripts/netProbe.ts` is the existing full handshake probe — reference for the WS client shape.)

## Critical files / commands

- `server/fly.toml`, `server/Dockerfile` — the committed deploy config (unchanged).
- `scripts/netProbe.ts` — the existing WS probe used for the v0.13.0 prod validation (reference for the close-code check).
- [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md) — the runbook this follows (deploy command, health check, troubleshooting table).

## Verification

- `fly deploy` reports a successful release; `/health` returns 200 `{"ok":true}`; the WS close-code probe confirms the deployed server is v2 (4000 on `protocol:2`+bad ticket, 4001 on `protocol:1`).
- Definitive end-to-end confirmation is the **manual pass** below: open `https://monecraft.vercel.app`, guest sign-in → create an online world → it connects (WELCOME).

## Out of scope (your timing, unblocked by this)

- The **manual 2-browser gameplay pass** on the live deploy — board a boat together, see arrows fly, each earn a distinct advancement, kick a guest, open a cloud world on a second device. (Not headless-automatable; the recurring project debt.)
- Cutting **v0.14.0** — version bump + roll `CHANGELOG [Unreleased] → [0.14.0]` + `chore(release)` commit + annotated tag, matching the v0.13.0 flow.

content.text: The pattern is clear. Fly's equivalent of Vercel auto-deploy is a GitHub Actions workflow that runs `fly deploy` on push to `main`, authed by a **Fly deploy token** kept as a GitHub secret. Let me create the workflow (matching your `ci.yml` style):

# Auto-deploy the Bun game server to Fly on every push to main — the Fly
# equivalent of Vercel's git integration (which deploys the web app). Only runs
# when server-relevant code changes (the server bundles the shared engine under
# lib/), so a docs- or web-only push doesn't rebuild it. Auth is a Fly deploy
# token stored as the FLY_API_TOKEN repo secret (see docs/deploy.md).
name: Deploy game server

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "server/**"
      - "lib/**"
      - "package.json"
      - "bun.lock"
      - ".github/workflows/fly-deploy.yml"

# One deploy at a time; don't cancel an in-flight rollout (Fly does its own).
concurrency:
  group: fly-deploy
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: superfly/flyctl-actions/setup-flyctl@master
      # --remote-only builds on Fly's builder (no Docker on the runner). Same
      # config/dockerfile as the manual `fly deploy` in docs/deploy.md.
      - run: flyctl deploy --config server/fly.toml --dockerfile server/Dockerfile --remote-only
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}
